title: GitHub - Vumb-VibeCoder/super-computer-agent: Read-only Windows MCP server: delta canvas, pixel grid + UI Automation tree to cut agent vision tokens.
excerpt: Read-only Windows MCP server: delta canvas, pixel grid + UI Automation tree to cut agent vision tokens. - Vumb-VibeCoder/super-computer-agent
content_html:
A read-only, observation-only MCP server for Windows that bundles four screen-observation capabilities into one package — it never clicks or types anything.

Capability What it does Main tools
Screenshot Captures the whole desktop (all monitors) to PNG screenshot, view_image
UI tree Windows UI Automation tree of a window (JSON: index, parent, type, name, rect) ui_list_windows, ui_get_tree
Live pixel grid Raw color grid of the screen plus a log of changed regions, fused with the UI tree to label what changed live_start, grid_now, ui_fuse, changes_since, wait_stable, crop, zoom, ...
Fovea Sends one keyframe, then only the changed parts (patch, scroll, recall an earlier scene, precise zoomed reads) to use far fewer image tokens fovea_start, fovea_step, fovea_look, fovea_expect, fovea_status, fovea_stop

28 tools total, no input injection of any kind.

Installation

Requires Windows 10/11 and Python >= 3.10.

git clone <repo> super-computer-agent
cd super-computer-agent
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
super-computer-agent doctor

doctor checks dependencies, takes a trial screenshot, and spins up the server as a smoke test (verified on the development machine: 28 tools).

Fovea and pixel-grid need a license key — everything else works right away. Their core is closed-source and license-gated (see License); without a key, fovea_start/live_start fail with a clear error, but screenshot and the UI tree still work.

  • Free 1-day trial key: Email hoanggiabao40478@gmail.com with the subject SCA 1-day trial (or open a quick GitHub issue / DM me on Reddit) and I will send back a .lickey file valid for 24 hours so you can test fovea and the pixel grid locally.
  • Longer / commercial keys: Email hoanggiabao40478@gmail.com with how many machines/concurrent threads you need.

Once you have the file, either set the environment variable:

set SCA_LICENSE_KEY=C:\path\to\your.lickey

or drop the file at the default path %USERPROFILE%\.super-computer-agent\license.lickey.

Running

super-computer-agent serve                      :: stdio (default, for an MCP client)
super-computer-agent serve --transport streamable-http --port 8000

super-computer-agent screenshot -o shot.png     :: usable without MCP
super-computer-agent windows                    :: JSON list of visible windows
super-computer-agent tree 66438 --depth 3       :: UIA tree for a given hwnd

MCP client configuration (e.g. Claude Desktop):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "super-computer-agent": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "super_computer_agent", "serve"],
      "env": { "SCA_OUTPUT_DIR": "C:\\Users\\you\\sca-output" }
    }
  }
}

Environment variables:

Variable Meaning
SCA_OUTPUT_DIR Where images are written (screenshots/, fovea_live/, pixel_grid/). Defaults to ./outputs relative to the working directory, so set an absolute path when running from an MCP client. view_image only opens files inside this directory.
SCA_SCREENSHOT free disables screenshot's guard-rail (the tiering tags and hints still apply).
SCA_ALLOWED_PROCESSES Optional. ;-separated list of executables (name or full path) allowed to be listed/read by the UI tree. Empty = every non-sensitive window.

Coordinating the tools

Fovea is the default; a full-screen screenshot is the last resort, for when things are genuinely hard to read any other way. Priority order: fovea_step -> fovea_look (precise reading) -> ui_fuse (element names/positions, as text) -> wait_stable (wait) -> a new keyframe (fovea_start) -> only then screenshot. Details and the exact conditions for using screenshot: docs/WORKFLOW.md. The server enforces this ordering through tiering tags on tool descriptions, NEXT: hints after results, warnings on repeated probing, and a guard-rail on screenshot (it requires a valid reason, checked against the current session; set SCA_SCREENSHOT=free to disable it). See the last section of docs/WORKFLOW.md.

Using fovea (summary)

  1. Call fovea_start() once, then fovea_step() whenever you need to look at the screen.
  2. The first call, and every scene change, is a KEY (a full image, opened with view_image). Subsequent calls are just delta commands (COPY, LOW, SCROLL, RECALL) applied to the canvas in order.
  3. Fovea is an approximate image. To read small text/numbers precisely, use fovea_look(x, y, w, h). To check "did this region change" without spending image tokens, use fovea_expect first.

Full spec: docs/FOVEA_PROTOCOL.md. Measurements: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

How it works

Fovea (fovea_start -> fovea_step): instead of sending a full screenshot every time (expensive — models are billed by pixel count), it sends only what changed. Fovea is not a rewrite from scratch — it is an upgrade layer wrapped directly around the older grid-compression core (canvas_v6/v7/delta2/delta3), adding a 64-frame scene memory (RECALL #k), precise 1:1 zoomed reads (fovea_look), an HWND lock plus a lightweight UIA signature check to catch focus-switch races, and a hard cap on the cell store.

  • First call, and every time the scene changes: a KEY — a full image (the keyframe).
  • Every call after that is just the delta needed to update the previous canvas: COPY (real pixels copied tile-by-tile from a named image), LOW (a blurred low-resolution preview that sharpens on later steps), SCROLL (a region shifted up/down by N px), and RECALL — the centerpiece of fovea: it remembers a handful of recently-seen scenes, so alt-tabbing between two familiar windows costs a few tokens ("go back to scene #k") instead of a fresh keyframe.
  • A lightweight UIA signature scan runs on the first two tree tiers (up to 40 controls) every step; if it changes while pixels are static, fovea fires a KEYFRAME uia within one step instead of waiting on a pixel threshold. If the canvas itself changes drastically (>=60% of cells) while UIA stays quiet, it fires a separate KEYFRAME canvas — the two failure modes are tracked as distinct counters in fovea_status.
  • Minimized/closed windows, hwnd=0, black frames, and mss capture errors all resolve to WAIT (0 extra tokens, canvas and history untouched) instead of being treated as valid content or crashing.

The frame-diffing algorithm itself is closed-source, shipped only as a compiled .pyd.

Pixel grid (live_start/grid_now/ui_fuse/...): a different trade-off — instead of a real image, the screen becomes a grid of colored characters (one character per tile, encoding hue + brightness), which is far cheaper for a model to read as a general layout overview than a picture.

  • tree_set/ui_fuse takes the Windows UI Automation tree (element names, types, coordinates) and overlays index numbers onto the matching grid tiles, so the model sees shape+color and "this tile is the Submit button, index 42" at once.
  • A background thread watches for pixel changes plus Windows' SetWinEventHook (focus, window open/close); changes_since / watch_until_change / wait_idle report what changed and where without re-capturing the whole screen on every poll.
  • verify_action compares the real event (pixel + OS event) against what was expected (change/none/new_window/close) after a click, so the model can tell "that worked as expected" from "something's off" instead of assuming a click landed.

This module's core is closed-source in full (not just the hot path), also shipped only as a compiled .pyd.

Both cores are gated by the offline Ed25519 license check described in Installation and License; the gate runs inside the compiled binary itself, not only in the public wrapper around it.

Benchmarks

Measured on this machine. Full numbers and methodology: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

Fovea is not a rewrite — it is an upgrade layer wrapped directly around the old canvas grid-compression core. The old canvas build, run in real-world use on Windows, had four bottlenecks: switching between familiar windows/tabs cost ~600 tokens every time with no memory of prior scenes; small adjacent characters on the shrunk 960px grid were unreadable, forcing the model to guess; a focus-switch race (changing windows in the wrong millisecond, or the UIA tree changing while pixels stayed still) could apply the wrong delta or take up to 8 steps to notice; and long sessions grew RAM and the cell store without bound, while black or minimized-window frames still got written into history as if they were real content. Fovea fixes all four by keeping the old grid core and adding a 64-frame scene memory (RECALL #k), a precise 1:1 zoom tool (fovea_look), an HWND lock plus a lightweight UIA signature check, and a hard cap on the cell store.

Measurement Old canvas (baseline) Fovea (patched) What causes the difference
Avg tokens / step 521 ~138 (~73.5% lower) 64-frame RECALL + HWND lock recapture on a detected race
Returning to a known window ~600 tok <60 tok (best case 3-15 tok) Hash-matches a cached frame from the 64-frame memory (22 RECALL hits measured)
Reading small text precisely not available (guessing on the 960px grid) exact 1:1 region crop fovea_look zooms only the region that needs reading
Window-mismatch errors (KEYFRAME race) 3 (rising to 7 once RECALL was added) 0 HWND identity lock forces a recapture when a mismatch is detected
Detecting a silent UIA change (pixels static) up to 8 steps 1 step Lightweight 2-tier UIA signature scan (<=40 nodes, 0-29 ms) every step
Recovering when the canvas changes >=60% of cells (UIA static) full keyframe (~700-1000+ tok) targeted KEYFRAME canvas only Separate UIA vs. canvas recovery channels, tracked individually in fovea_status
Processing time / step UIA scan cost not controlled ~51 ms (static) / ~100 ms (full: grab 51ms + png 2ms + step 47ms) mss capture fully decoupled from pywinauto
Minimized window (-32000) / hwnd=0 treated as valid, costs a 524-tok keyframe WAIT (0 tokens), canvas unchanged Detects IsWindow=False, empty rect, or hwnd=0
Black frame / mss error written into history (767 tok) or raised RuntimeError WAIT (0 tokens); returning to a real frame costs 1 token Black frames under 3 consecutive steps are ignored (3+ steps is treated as real content)
500-step soak test (1080p, always-new content) RAM +19 MB / 88,110 cells, growing linearly RAM +9 MB / 28,860 cells, flattens after step 300 Cell store capped at 30,000 (oldest evicted), frame history capped at 64, PNGs capped at 60

Everything that was already solid at the old canvas grid layer carries over unchanged: 0% long-run state drift (0/46 checkpoints) and 0% stale OCR (0/248 rows) in a 125-second dynamic-spreadsheet stress test, and correct physical-pixel/DPI handling at Windows 150% scale (UIA and the captured frame both resolve to the same physical 1920x1080 pixels, mapped to the 960x544 canvas at exactly a factor of 2).

Security

  • No tool controls the mouse or keyboard. test_server.py asserts this.
  • UI tree (ui_list_windows, ui_get_tree, ui_fuse): hides sensitive windows (password managers, banking apps, UAC, credential UI), skips processes running as admin or whose permission level can't be determined (fail closed), masks password fields, and caps results at 500 nodes / 6 levels.
  • Screenshot, fovea, and the pixel grid do NOT filter content: they capture whatever is on screen, including any sensitive window that's open. Don't run the server when something you don't want the model to see is visible.
  • Text found in the UI tree or in images is untrusted data and may contain prompt injection.
  • The server only listens on 127.0.0.1 by default over HTTP; there is no authentication — don't expose it to a network.

Known limitations

  • Fovea and the pixel grid capture the primary monitor; screenshot captures every monitor.
  • Only tested on Windows. Chromium/Electron apps may expose only a handful of UIA nodes (a Chromium-based browser tested during development showed only 4 nodes in the tree).
  • The CI workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml has not yet been run on GitHub.

Testing

python -m pytest -q                        :: full suite, no display needed (35 passed, 1 skipped)
set SCA_INTEGRATION=1 && python -m pytest -q -m integration   :: adds the tests that use a real display/window

Structure

src/super_computer_agent/
  cli.py  server.py  host.py        CLI, MCP server, plugin adapter
  coordination.py                   priority tiering, NEXT hints, screenshot guard-rail
  uia.py                            UI Automation tree (read-only)
  screenshot.py                     desktop capture
  licensing/                        offline Ed25519 license-key check (public key only)
  plugins/fovea_live.py             thin loader for the compiled fovea core — public, AGPL-3.0
  plugins/pixel_grid.py             thin loader for the compiled pixel_grid core — public, AGPL-3.0
  plugins/_compiled/fovea_live.pyd  fovea core (built on the old canvas_v6/v7/delta2/delta3) — compiled, proprietary
  plugins/_compiled/pixel_grid.pyd  pixel_grid core — compiled, proprietary
tests/   docs/

Licensing note: plugins/fovea_live.py's compiled core and plugins/pixel_grid.py's compiled core are not covered by the AGPL-3.0 license below — see License.

  • Everything except the two modules below is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0). See LICENSE.

Reverse engineering, decompiling, and disassembling them is prohibited. Terms: PROPRIETARY_EULA.md.

blocks.html_en: Fovea is not a rewrite — it is an upgrade layer wrapped directly around the old canvas grid-compression core. The old canvas build, run in real-world use on Windows, had four bottlenecks: switching between familiar windows/tabs cost ~600 tokens every time with no memory of prior scenes; small adjacent characters on the shrunk 960px grid were unreadable, forcing the model to guess; a focus-switch race (changing windows in the wrong millisecond, or the UIA tree changing while pixels stayed still) could apply the wrong delta or take up to 8 steps to notice; and long sessions grew RAM and the cell store without bound, while black or minimized-window frames still got written into history as if they were real content. Fovea fixes all four by keeping the old grid core and adding a 64-frame scene memory (RECALL #k), a precise 1:1 zoom tool (fovea_look), an HWND lock plus a lightweight UIA signature check, and a hard cap on the cell store.

content_html_zh:
A read-only, observation-only MCP server for Windows that bundles four screen-observation capabilities into one package — it never clicks or types anything.

能力 它的作用 Main tools
截屏 Captures the whole desktop (all monitors) to PNG screenshot, view_image
UI tree Windows UI Automation tree of a window (JSON: index, parent, type, name, rect) ui_list_windows, ui_get_tree
Live pixel grid Raw color grid of the screen plus a log of changed regions, fused with the UI tree to label what changed live_start, grid_now, ui_fuse, changes_since, wait_stable, crop, zoom, ...
Fovea Sends one keyframe, then only the changed parts (patch, scroll, recall an earlier scene, precise zoomed reads) to use far fewer image tokens fovea_start, fovea_step, fovea_look, fovea_expect, fovea_status, fovea_stop

28 tools total, no input injection of any kind.

安装

Requires Windows 10/11 and Python >= 3.10.

git clone <repo> super-computer-agent
cd super-computer-agent
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
super-computer-agent doctor

doctor checks dependencies, takes a trial screenshot, and spins up the server as a smoke test (verified on the development machine: 28 tools).

Fovea and pixel-grid need a license key — everything else works right away. Their core is closed-source and license-gated (see License); without a key, fovea_start/live_start fail with a clear error, but screenshot and the UI tree still work.

  • Free 1-day trial key: Email hoanggiabao40478@gmail.com with the subject SCA 1-day trial (or open a quick GitHub issue / DM me on Reddit) and I will send back a .lickey file valid for 24 hours so you can test fovea and the pixel grid locally.
  • Longer / commercial keys: Email hoanggiabao40478@gmail.com with how many machines/concurrent threads you need.

Once you have the file, either set the environment variable:

set SCA_LICENSE_KEY=C:\path\to\your.lickey

or drop the file at the default path %USERPROFILE%\.super-computer-agent\license.lickey.

跑步

super-computer-agent serve                      :: stdio (default, for an MCP client)
super-computer-agent serve --transport streamable-http --port 8000

super-computer-agent screenshot -o shot.png     :: usable without MCP
super-computer-agent windows                    :: JSON list of visible windows
super-computer-agent tree 66438 --depth 3       :: UIA tree for a given hwnd

MCP client configuration (e.g. Claude Desktop):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "super-computer-agent": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "super_computer_agent", "serve"],
      "env": { "SCA_OUTPUT_DIR": "C:\\Users\\you\\sca-output" }
    }
  }
}

SCA_OUTPUT_DIR Where images are written (screenshots/, fovea_live/, pixel_grid/). Defaults to ./outputs relative to the working directory, so set an absolute path when running from an MCP client. view_image only opens files inside this directory.
SCA_SCREENSHOT free disables screenshot's guard-rail (the tiering tags and hints still apply).

Coordinating the tools

Fovea is the default; a full-screen screenshot is the last resort, for when things are genuinely hard to read any other way. Priority order: fovea_step -> fovea_look (precise reading) -> ui_fuse (element names/positions, as text) -> wait_stable (wait) -> a new keyframe (fovea_start) -> only then screenshot. Details and the exact conditions for using screenshot: docs/WORKFLOW.md. The server enforces this ordering through tiering tags on tool descriptions, NEXT: hints after results, warnings on repeated probing, and a guard-rail on screenshot (it requires a valid reason, checked against the current session; set SCA_SCREENSHOT=free to disable it). See the last section of docs/WORKFLOW.md.

Using fovea (summary)

  1. Call fovea_start() once, then fovea_step() whenever you need to look at the screen.
  2. The first call, and every scene change, is a KEY (a full image, opened with view_image). Subsequent calls are just delta commands (COPY, LOW, SCROLL, RECALL) applied to the canvas in order.
  3. Fovea is an approximate image. To read small text/numbers precisely, use fovea_look(x, y, w, h). To check "did this region change" without spending image tokens, use fovea_expect first.

Full spec: docs/FOVEA_PROTOCOL.md. Measurements: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

它是如何运作的

Fovea (fovea_start -> fovea_step): instead of sending a full screenshot every time (expensive — models are billed by pixel count), it sends only what changed. Fovea is not a rewrite from scratch — it is an upgrade layer wrapped directly around the older grid-compression core (canvas_v6/v7/delta2/delta3), adding a 64-frame scene memory (RECALL #k), precise 1:1 zoomed reads (fovea_look), an HWND lock plus a lightweight UIA signature check to catch focus-switch races, and a hard cap on the cell store.

  • First call, and every time the scene changes: a KEY — a full image (the keyframe).
  • Every call after that is just the delta needed to update the previous canvas: COPY (real pixels copied tile-by-tile from a named image), LOW (a blurred low-resolution preview that sharpens on later steps), SCROLL (a region shifted up/down by N px), and RECALL — the centerpiece of fovea: it remembers a handful of recently-seen scenes, so alt-tabbing between two familiar windows costs a few tokens ("go back to scene #k") instead of a fresh keyframe.
  • A lightweight UIA signature scan runs on the first two tree tiers (up to 40 controls) every step; if it changes while pixels are static, fovea fires a KEYFRAME uia within one step instead of waiting on a pixel threshold. If the canvas itself changes drastically (>=60% of cells) while UIA stays quiet, it fires a separate KEYFRAME canvas — the two failure modes are tracked as distinct counters in fovea_status.
  • Minimized/closed windows, hwnd=0, black frames, and mss capture errors all resolve to WAIT (0 extra tokens, canvas and history untouched) instead of being treated as valid content or crashing.

The frame-diffing algorithm itself is closed-source, shipped only as a compiled .pyd.

Pixel grid (live_start/grid_now/ui_fuse/...): a different trade-off — instead of a real image, the screen becomes a grid of colored characters (one character per tile, encoding hue + brightness), which is far cheaper for a model to read as a general layout overview than a picture.

  • tree_set/ui_fuse takes the Windows UI Automation tree (element names, types, coordinates) and overlays index numbers onto the matching grid tiles, so the model sees shape+color and "this tile is the Submit button, index 42" at once.
  • A background thread watches for pixel changes plus Windows' SetWinEventHook (focus, window open/close); changes_since / watch_until_change / wait_idle report what changed and where without re-capturing the whole screen on every poll.
  • verify_action compares the real event (pixel + OS event) against what was expected (change/none/new_window/close) after a click, so the model can tell "that worked as expected" from "something's off" instead of assuming a click landed.

This module's core is closed-source in full (not just the hot path), also shipped only as a compiled .pyd.

Both cores are gated by the offline Ed25519 license check described in Installation and License; the gate runs inside the compiled binary itself, not only in the public wrapper around it.

基准测试

Measured on this machine. Full numbers and methodology: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

Fovea is not a rewrite — it is an upgrade layer wrapped directly around the old canvas grid-compression core. The old canvas build, run in real-world use on Windows, had four bottlenecks: switching between familiar windows/tabs cost ~600 tokens every time with no memory of prior scenes; small adjacent characters on the shrunk 960px grid were unreadable, forcing the model to guess; a focus-switch race (changing windows in the wrong millisecond, or the UIA tree changing while pixels stayed still) could apply the wrong delta or take up to 8 steps to notice; and long sessions grew RAM and the cell store without bound, while black or minimized-window frames still got written into history as if they were real content. Fovea fixes all four by keeping the old grid core and adding a 64-frame scene memory (RECALL #k), a precise 1:1 zoom tool (fovea_look), an HWND lock plus a lightweight UIA signature check, and a hard cap on the cell store.

Everything that was already solid at the old canvas grid layer carries over unchanged: 0% long-run state drift (0/46 checkpoints) and 0% stale OCR (0/248 rows) in a 125-second dynamic-spreadsheet stress test, and correct physical-pixel/DPI handling at Windows 150% scale (UIA and the captured frame both resolve to the same physical 1920x1080 pixels, mapped to the 960x544 canvas at exactly a factor of 2).

安全

  • No tool controls the mouse or keyboard. test_server.py asserts this.
  • UI tree (ui_list_windows, ui_get_tree, ui_fuse): hides sensitive windows (password managers, banking apps, UAC, credential UI), skips processes running as admin or whose permission level can't be determined (fail closed), masks password fields, and caps results at 500 nodes / 6 levels.
  • Screenshot, fovea, and the pixel grid do NOT filter content: they capture whatever is on screen, including any sensitive window that's open. Don't run the server when something you don't want the model to see is visible.
  • Text found in the UI tree or in images is untrusted data and may contain prompt injection.
  • The server only listens on 127.0.0.1 by default over HTTP; there is no authentication — don't expose it to a network.

已知的限制

  • Fovea and the pixel grid capture the primary monitor; screenshot captures every monitor.
  • Only tested on Windows. Chromium/Electron apps may expose only a handful of UIA nodes (a Chromium-based browser tested during development showed only 4 nodes in the tree).
  • The CI workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml has not yet been run on GitHub.
